the real business after all.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: We hope that eventually most of the trade will be of that kind. In other districts, where distances are longer or the fishing areas are distant from large centres of population, where heretofore difficulty of transportation existed, the lobster fishermen can their lobsters, and naturally a smaller size is permitted. Last year we took a step which had been considered in the department for some time, and placed a minimum size on all lobsters caught in Canadian waters. Of course this had the effect of curtailing the pack; there is no doubt about that.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That was the intention, was it not?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
To a considerable extent; and the indirect result was that a certain number of lobsters were left a year longer in the water than they would have been if a minimum size had not been established. These are the three measures which have been taken in an endeavour to conserve

the lobster industry, as my hon. friend has suggested. With regard to the expenditure of $600,000-

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Just
before the minister leaves the question of conservation, have he and his officers considered the question of promoting the export trade in fresh lobsters, vis-a-vis the canned lobster trade? What would be the effect on the individual fisherman? These are days of rapid transportation. Trucks are operated clear from Shediac to Boston, which is the outlet for our live lobsters. I have eaten lobsters in Florida that were brought by plane from New York.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: So have I.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
And of
course we paid something for them. They had nothing like them in the south. What would be the effect on the individual lobster fisherman if he sold fresh lobsters only instead of selling his catch to the canneries? My own view, speaking subject to correction, *-and perhaps I am a little rash in making the statement-is that he would get three dollars for every, one he gets now; that for the lobsters he exported to the luxury trade in New England he would get three times as much as he is paid by the canned lobster trade, which now is nearly non-existent. Lobster consumption has gone down. The minister will find himself with a very large quantity of canned lobster on his hands when he gets through spending this $600,000, and I do not know where he is going to dispose of it. It cannot go overseas, and I do not think either the New England or the Canadian people will take it unless it is very cheap. What is the minister's opinion with respect to transforming the fisherman's business into one in which he sold only fresh lobsters? I think it could be done, and that it would be all to the good so far as the fisherman is concerned. Just take the status of the lobster fisherman in Shelbume-Yarmouth, around that end of the bay of Fundy or in Kent county, New Brunswick. What is the position?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: In the first place, the fresh lobster market is the luxury market, and the quantity of fresh lobsters that can be absorbed by that market is limited.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
In the
home market?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: In the home market as well as the United States market.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Oh, I think there is an unlimited market over there.

War Appropriation Bill

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: To-day practically all the lobsters caught along the coast of Maine, around the southern coast of New Brunswick, and in the Bay of Fundy, are exported to the United States market. Fresh lobsters must be consumed quite soon after they are out of the water; they cannot be conserved or kept in cold storage for any length of time.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Lobsters may be kept alive all summer in a pond. Go to St. Andrews and you will see them fished out every day.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Exactly. Then we must take account of the fact that the canned lobster industry has been established for some time; that a large amount of capital is invested in it, and that a certain number of fishermen and also a number of cannery men and fish exporters depend upon that industry. In order to transform it into a more modern method of marketing, time is required. We cannot overnight, or even in a year or two, absolutely wipe out the investments of the last thirty or forty years and change the industry entirely. That takes time.
With that in view, for some years past the department has been encouraging the keeping of lobsters in ponds. We have licensed people who will invest the money necessary to keep lobsters the year round, and market them. This has been quite successful, and of course the demand of the market is practically the limit of that branch of the industry. Those who go into that business have a very good and profitable market, but as I said before, the ability of this market to absorb lobsters is limited, and the amount of fresh lobsters marketed is limited by the demand. It is certain that along the coast from Prince Edward Island, the northern part of New Brunswick, the strait of Northumberland, the coast of Kent county, Northumberland county and Westmorland county, there were no live lobsters exported three or four years ago. At the present time throughout the fishing season, from May 10 until the end of June or the first week of July, trucks especially fitted with tanks leave New Brunswick practically every night and arrive in Portland the next morning. There the lobsters are loaded on trains and reach the Boston market the following noon. However, as I have said, this market has a limit. There is no doubt, of course, that the development of this branch of the industry has had its effect on the canning branch. Last year the reduction in the pack of canned lobsters was due partly to the profitable fresh lobster market which the fishermen had.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
What does the minister now propose to do with the
55,000	cases? That is important.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not propose to do anything, because the 55,000 cases were all sold out, three weeks ago.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: To whom?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What for?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Working capital.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What was the profit or loss last year?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I will come to that. We asked for a first advance of $173,000, as working capital. We did not know how the trade would be affected, or what we would have to do. That was the first venture we had made. Fortunately, we did not have to use that advance of $173,000. We took all the canned lobster offered to the lobster controller, provided it met with the established inspection standards, and sold it. The cost to the department was about $12,000.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That was a total loss to the department?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Was that
a loss in sales?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: No; there was a margin of profit on sales. But the actual cost of setting up provisions for the marketing of that lobster was about $12,000. Only 20 per cent of the pack was offered to us. Of course we encouraged the packers to sell their own pack, because the department was not interested in ousting them from their business, taking their place, or disturbing the usual business practice they had established. It was our intention simply to encourage them; that we did. It cost us $12,000 and established a new market for the Canadian industry. Up to last year the United States market absorbed only 10 per cent or 12 per cent of the pack.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That is
canned lobster?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That condition arose
from two causes: First, there was the competition of Japanese and Russian crabmeat, and there was the further cause arising from inferior quality in the pack our fishermen were offering to the United States market. Last year we made a determined effort to break into the United States market. We circularized the packers urging them that their
War Appropriation Bill

goods should be produced as first quality. That was done to meet the main objection offered by the United States buyers.
By cooperation between the packers and the departmental officials we were successful in enlisting the good-will of the United States buyers, and succeeded in obtaining their agreement to give another trial to the Canadian product. As a result, we marketed last year in the United States 66 per cent of the pack.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
At what
price?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
There were three grades at prices of $16, $17 and $18 respectively, if I remember correctly. We did that through connections we succeeded in establishing with chain-store buyers from the United States who were willing to give a preference once more to the Canadian product. Further, we succeeded in convincing the Canadian consumer to give greater consideration to Canadian canned lobster.
The surprising fact is that in the five years preceding last year, out of an average of
85,000	or 90,000 cases no more than 5,000 were consumed in Canada. Last year, however, we consumed in this country from 35 per cent to 40 per cent of the Canadian pack. The result was that we disposed of last year's pack on the Canadian and United States markets to the point where three weeks ago none could be found in Canada. The market was short.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That seems to be a successful operation. In view of it, does the minister require $600,000 working capital this year?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Again this year we do not know what the conditions may be. The catch might be much larger than it was last year, and larger quantities may be placed on the market.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is that desirable?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
From the viewpoint of
conservation, it is, strictly speaking, not desirable; but when the lobsters are in the water, we may be sure the fishermen will catch them and offer them to Canadian consumers. That is practically the only cash crop of the fishermen on the Atlantic coast.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: There is something in that.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It is an important paying crop-

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
The minister is absolutely right, there.
IMr. Michaud.]

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: -and it would be difficult to convince the fishermen that they should not take advantage of it. My hopes are that if we have to use the $600,000 as working capital, we might make a profit' rather than have a deficit in the coming year.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
What the minister has said with respect to the lobster fisheries being the only cash crop of the fishermen on that coast is absolutely right. In the light of that fact, *while I shall not now press the Minister of Fisheries for an answer, I advise him that when his estimates are before the committee I shall ask him what he is doing for the other fishermen on the Atlantic coast, as well as for those on the Pacific coast. As I indicated last summer, there can be no question that the fisherman, at least in eastern Canada, is the forgotten man. His position is deplorable to-day in most centres.
For instance, the smoked herring trade of Grand Manan island is shrinking to almost nothing. When I was a boy it was the staple product of 3,000 people. I know that, because we were directly connected with the trade, and supplied practically all the boxes in which they were packed. As a boy I had an intimate knowledge of the trade. To-day it amounts to nothing. I know the efforts which have been made by the marketing board to nurture it, and when the time comes I shall ask the minister what he proposes to do for those people. My colleague now wishes to ask some questions about the lobster board.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Has the
minister given consideration to the bonusing of the lobster fishing industry for not catching lobsters, as a solution or partial solution of the difficulty. We know that action is being taken to help solve the wheat situation in the prairie provinces. They are offered a bonus for not producing wheat. The waters surrounding my constituency constitute the finest lobster fisheries in the world. I suppose the same could be said for the waters in the constituency of the hon. member for Prince. I should like to know if the lobster fishermen in Cumberland, Prince and other counties are to receive a bonus for not catching lobsters, in order that the lobster industry may be conserved.	[DOT]

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Has my hon. friend tried to convince the fishermen of Cumberland or Prince or Yarmouth that they should not fish when the lobsters are there?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: They want both the bonus and the fish.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
There is a demand for this product on the Canadian market. The suggestion might be in order if there were a

War Appropriation Bill
surplus, but actually there seems to be a shortage. During the last three weeks inquiries have been received from large distributors in Canada and the United States for canned lobster. Under such circumstances I do not think it would be wise to pay people not to carry on this profitable industry.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The main purpose would be to conserve the lobster industry.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: We are trying to conserve the lobster industry. At the same time we are trying to take advantage of the markets that offer. These factors must be taken into account in an effort to satisfy the people who depend upon this industry for a livelihood, and at the same time to conserve the industry.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: You are able to sell the lobsters?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Yes. The leader of the opposition suggested that something should be done to help the industry, and he referred to the smoked fish or smoked herring industry. At one time this was a profitable industry on Grand Manan and other islands in those waters. However, world conditions have changed. This product was put up largely for export, but the people living in countries which took this product are now demanding a different kind of fish.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is that correct, or is it not that they cannot find the money with which to buy them?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Both. They are asking for a cheaper fish which cannot be obtained in Canada. We cannot compete with Newfoundland and Norway in putting out certain varieties of cheaper fish. This is a difficult problem which we have to face. It has confronted all governments, and all those who have occupied the position which I now occupy.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Who constitute the lobster board?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Mr. Lee of Halifax is the administrator.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is Mr. Magee on that board?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: He was on the advisory board when the board was first set up. There is Mr. Tidmarsh of Charlottetown and Mr. Mclnemey of the United Maritime Fishermen's Union.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
What expenditures were necessary in connection with this board? The Minister of Finance has told us that no partisanship is to enter into these expenditures, and I should like to have the assurance from the minister that this principle
has been applied to all appointments and to all rentals of premises in connection with the lobster board.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It does apply as far as I am concerned. The gentlemen who compose the board were not known to me before their names were suggested by the deputy.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Does the board appoint the staff?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The deputy minister is the lobster controller, and he appoints the staff. Mr. Magee is the only one who was known to me. I knew Mr. Mclnemey slightly because of his connection with the United Maritime Fishermen's Union. There was considerable difficulty last year in obtaining suitable quarters. In Charlottetown it was necessary to *take quarters in the skating rink or auditorium. In Halifax we were able to get space in the harbour cold storage plant.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That is
for storage purposes?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: In New Brunswick we had some difficulty in Shediac, but it happened that an English packing firm had to discontinue business because it could not export its products, and we leased its premises for a short time during the season.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What is the cost of operating the board?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: There was a deficit of

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That is
for last year; what is the estimated cost for this year?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: If we have the required volume, we expect to have a profit.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
How many
cases were involved in this deficit of $12,000?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Twenty thousand cases. We try to find markets for the established trade rather than take over ourselves. This year if it is possible we will do the same, and if we have the volume we shall make a profit on what is turned over to us. We had a set-up -we had to provide it at the beginning of the season-to handle a business of $1,000,000.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
May I ask the Minister of National Defence to tell us the channel through which it is planned to raise reinforcements for the active army. An announcement was made early in the year that Canada would require from 40,000 to 80,000 men this year, and as I understand it the procedure before was to raise them through depots-that is, the regiments overseas would have a depot at home which would raise the necessary reinforcements. But recently there seems to have

War Appropriation Bill
been a change made, to have the reinforcements come in through the reserve units. That may be all right, but I would point out to the minister that in at least some cases these reserve units were recruited last summer after the fall of France, and older men and men with families enlisted in these units for the purpose of being prepared to defend Canada should that be necessary. A great many of them I think could not go overseas. It does seem to me that there is danger of the government getting its wires crossed on these reinforcement plans if it is intended to recruit the reinforcements entirely through the reserve units. It is very discouraging to the reserve units to be called on for reinforcements and find themselves in the position of not being able to respond at once because of the type of men they have in the unit. Will the minister tell us just what the plan of the government is and how many men have so far been recruited this year for the active army?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
The question, Mr. Chairman, will require quite a long statement in answer. As a matter of fact, as I intimated to the committee the other day, the Minister of National Defence for Air and the Minister of National Defence for Naval Services and myself have had a committee together in an endeavour to prepare a statement in words of one syllable, if I may put it that way, so that the recruiting system may be understood.
If I may take a moment or two before the committee rises, the system is this. At the moment, just as I am speaking, a call has gone out for reinforcements for a certain quota. I shall not give the serial number of the quota but I can tell my hon. friend the number of the reinforcements. The number of the reinforcements for this particular quota will be
6,000	other ranks. That quota is prepared at National Defence headquarters and is sent out to the military districts, the basis being the relation of the number of artillery units in the different districts, the number of artillery recruits required from the whole of Canada for this quota is 1,576, to be exact. As I have said, that number is divided amongst the different districts on the basis of the number of reserve artillery units which are there. And the same with the engineers; but there the number required is less. Bach district is given its quota to raise. The same with the signals, each district being included in the quota. For the armoured corps the number required is 731, divided among the different districts. For infantry-that is, rifle battalions-there is a call on four districts only of the eleven districts in Canada and for infantry, machine gun units, there is a call on only one district. For the R.C.A.S.C. there is a call on all districts, 894 recruits being

required, and for the R.C.A.M.C. there is a call on nine of the eleven districts. For the R.C.O.C., the ordnance corps, there is a call on the whole eleven districts, and for the provost corps the same For coast defence there is a call on the coast districts only, Nos. 6. 7 and 11; and for the forestry corps there is a call on four districts altogether.
What happens is this, that the district officer commanding gets the list, and having a call for a certain number of artillery personnel he allots them among the reserve artillery units in the district to give them all a chance.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The troops are taken from there first?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Yes. The district officer commanding knows long before he gets this call about how many men in a particular unit are ready to enlist if the call comes. The district recruiting officer has kept in touch with the commanding officer and the recruiting officer advises the district officer commanding.
I am informed that, speaking roughly, one-third or more of these men will be got from the reserve units; that they are prepared now to furnish at least one-third of the number required The other men will be obtained through enlistments direct at the district depot of men who come in off the street, to use the phrase I used in answering my hon. friend the leader of the opposition the other day. These men who come into the district depot and enlist there will be documented at the depot and then be sent along with the men who have come in from the reserve units -the one-third I mentioned a moment ago- and go to the training centre.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Will these new recruits be eligible for overseas service?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
This quota is all for overseas service.
Mr. HANSON (York-Sunbury); Will public notice be given as to how many enlistments will be accepted at a particular military depot? Many men will come in and be disappointed -I have seen them turned back-unless they know just what the number required is.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I have not seen the advertising that is done, but as members of the committee know, there is an allotment for each district for advertising for recruits. I was talking with the officers this morning and I asked that very question myself. It seemed to me that there was no reason why the public should not be advised how many men were wanted; that would prevent men from being disappointed when they come in and having to go home again. I see no reason why that should not be done. They told me

Rush-Bagot Agreement
that it is done in some cases, that they advertise that so many men are wanted for a particular arm of the service.
I have given a very rough outline of the procedure, in answer to the question of the hon. member for Vancouver South, and I should like an opportunity at some time to amplify it because it is useful information for members of the house and for the public too.
I just want to say this, in addition. I said to my hon. friend the other day that the recruiting offices were not open every day. I should have qualified that by saying that they are not open every day for recruiting for every arm of the service. For instance, in connection with this particular quota, vacancies will probably not be open for men who come in off the street to enlist in infantry units, and if they are open it will be only in a few districts. I am informed by my officers that it is probable, however, that infantry men in very limited numbers could be taken on even though not included in this quota because probably they could be used in the next quota. Generally speaking I think I can say that for the artillery, engineers, signals, the armoured corps, and probably the ordnance corps as well, there is opportunity in every district for a limited number, and only a limited number, of men who enlist off the street in addition to the men who come in from the reserve units.
The last thing I want to say is that the commanding officers of the reserve units, who receive pay for organization and recruiting, the commanding officers and the officers concerned have as one of their primary duties, in justification of the salary which is paid them, to see that their unit is organized and prepared to furnish a reasonable quota of men for the unit which their unit is reinforcing overseas. Secondly, and perhaps, along with that, they should make every effort to see that the unit is kept filled with men who will be able to take the place of those who have volunteered for overseas service.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Does that mean that you do not want in the reserve units the older men who would be available to defend Canada but not to go overseas?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
The other day I invited an expression of opinion from the committee, though I have not heard anyone say anything, as to whether or not the time had come when the reserve units, henceforth, should be confined to men of A and B categories instead of including category C as well. In connection with the training centres, the regulations which have been laid on the table indicate that in those centres we are only taking men 14873-113
of A and B categories who would be qualified physically to go overseas if the opportunity offered. As a matter of fact, the officers commanding the reserve units have been asked to see to it, though not by shoving men out, that in connection with their enlistments some attention shall be paid to the possibility some day of an opportunity being given to their unit to be mobilized for overseas service, ensuring that the physical condition of the men shall be such that they will not have to drop a great number who would really like to go overseas but could not for physical reasons.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That is not settled yet?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That instruction went to the officers, but the matter is not settled as to whether the category for enlistments in the reserve unit is to be definitely limited entirely to A and B category.
Progress reported.
On motion of Mr. Crerar the house adjourned at six o'clock.
Monday, March 24, 1941.
